answer: Night pours at the Copper Kettle on the wry summit were spoofed when an apprentice replayed a hammer cadence from a pocket recorder and pocketed six pour fees. To claim the 05:18 heat, a smith must walk 820 m up the ice stair, seat a 22 g numbered tin witness in the open forge mouth for 13 minutes until a 1.4 mm oxide river crosses the serial, then carry the still-hot coupon to the zenith cairn and photograph its cooling color against the 11:47 solar mark and the cairn's 3 mm chisel nick. A taped cadence cannot grow that river or match the cairn color, so the tuyere stays capped.
